examples: The path is narrow.
The cat fit through the narrow gap.
We walked on a narrow bridge.
The street was so narrow that only one car could pass.
The bridge is too narrow for trucks.
A narrow stream ran through the field.

easy.def: Plants, animals, and all outdoor things not made by people.
examples: We like to walk in nature.
Birds and trees are part of nature.
We take care of nature.

more.def: Everything in the world not made by people, such as plants, animals, weather, and land.
examples: Hiking is a great way to enjoy nature.
She likes to draw things she finds in nature.
The power of nature can be seen in a big storm.

easy.def: A person who lives near you.
examples: My neighbor has a big dog.
Our neighbor gave us cookies.
I wave to my neighbor.

more.def: A person who lives next to or near you.
examples: Our neighbor waters our plants when we are away.
Canada is a neighbor of the United States.
The girl who sits next to me in class is a good neighbor.
I feel nervous on the first day of school.
The nervous cat hid under the bed.
I get nervous at the dentist.

more.def: Worried or a little afraid about something that is going to happen.
examples: She felt nervous before her piano recital.
He was nervous about meeting his new teacher.
The nervous horse jumped at every sound.
The mouse will nibble the cheese.
Fish nibble at the bread.
I nibble my cracker.

more.def: To eat something by taking small bites.
examples: The rabbit nibbled on a carrot.
Mice had nibbled a hole in the bag of grain.
The goat nibbled at my sleeve.

easy.def: Awake at night and asleep in the day.
examples: Owls are nocturnal.
Bats are nocturnal.
A nocturnal animal sleeps in the day.

more.def: Active at night and resting during the day.
examples: Bats are nocturnal animals that hunt insects after dark.
The zoo has a dark room for nocturnal animals.
Raccoons are nocturnal and often visit at night.
The noisy truck woke me up.
The noisy birds woke me up.
My baby brother is noisy.

more.def: Making a lot of loud sound, or full of loud sounds.
examples: The lunchroom is always noisy at noon.
The noisy fan kept me awake.
We moved away from the noisy road.

easy.def: Silly words or ideas that mean nothing.
examples: That funny poem is full of nonsense.
Stop that nonsense and eat.
The baby talks nonsense.

more.def: Words or ideas that are silly or have no meaning.
examples: He made us laugh by singing a song of pure nonsense.
The idea that the moon is made of cheese is nonsense.
The writer filled his book with funny nonsense words.
Did you notice my new haircut?
I noticed a bug on the wall.
Mom noticed my clean room.

more.def: To become aware of something by seeing, hearing, or feeling it.
examples: He noticed a small crack in the window.
Nobody noticed that the door was open.
I noticed that the days are getting shorter.

easy.def: Something in food that helps you grow.
examples: Milk has nutrients for strong bones.
Good food has nutrients.
Plants get nutrients from dirt.

more.def: A substance that living things need in order to grow and stay healthy.
examples: Plants take in nutrients from the soil through their roots.
Vegetables are full of important nutrients.
Fertilizer adds nutrients to the soil.
